_note: Battle royale loot (ours: Apex's loot tables are not published). Spots per place and what each spot holds, rarity weights, and what each rarity holds. Care-package guns per Season 30: the Kraber, the 30-30 and the L-STAR (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_11.md sections 10, 11, 15). Ammo amounts are one stack of the type, from src/config/ammo.json.
_density: The owner's note, 2026-09-16: 'there needs to be much less open space and more loot, like guns available'. The places now have buildings with floors and rooms to put loot IN (src/game/brpoi.ts), so a place carries a lot of spots (its tier's) and a spot holds about three items. The field keeps fewer, so the reason to go indoors is the loot: a landing that finds nothing is the complaint this fixes. The old single spotsPerPoi and itemsPerSpot are gone: a place's spot count is its tier's now, and a spot's contents are its kind's.
_tiers: Every place used to roll the same table from the same number of spots, so there was no reason to choose one place over another: you landed wherever the squad did and found the same match every time. A place has a tier now. The tier says how many spots it carries and multiplies the rarity weights above, and the result is normalised, so the owner tunes rarity in one place and the tiers stay relative to it. Ours: there is no published table to copy, but the shape (a few rich places, a lot of thin ones, one hot place a match) is what every battle royale does.
_places: Which place is which tier, by the id in src/game/br.ts's pois. East Ridge and West Town are high: the ridge is the hardest place on the map to leave and the town is the only one built room by room, so both should pay for the walk. The hub and the two yards are mid, because everybody lands on them anyway and they do not need a second reason. The four corner compounds are low, so crossing a corner is a choice and not a shortcut to a full kit.
_placeOrder: brmatch.ts hands the loot its places as bare x and z, so when a place arrives without its id we read the tier off this list by position. It is the order of the pois array in src/game/br.ts, and a place added there belongs here too.
_hot: One place a match is the Hot Zone: it rolls the hot tier instead of its own and holds a fully kitted gun. It is drawn from the match seed on its own stream, so a guest works out the same place the host did with nothing sent over the wire, and so that adding it did not shift a single one of the floor's other rolls. The radius is what the map rings; the loot sits within 34 m of a place's centre, so 40 m covers it with a margin.
_kitted: The prize in the Hot Zone: a gun that arrives with its attachments already fitted, so it is worth contesting rather than looting. The gun comes off the epic list but lies there gold, because what makes it gold is the kit and not the gun. Per slot we take the first mod on the prefer list that the gun can actually take, and the last one it is offered when it can take none of them. The hop-up list is empty on purpose: a gun's hop-ups are few and every one it is offered already fits it.
_spots: A spot is a place with a purpose, not a handful of independent dice. Every item used to roll on its own off the kinds table below, so a room could be four shield cells and nothing else and the next one two helmets: nothing read like a room. A spot picks one of these kinds and fills it. A gun rack holds a gun, a stack of the ammo THAT gun takes and a magazine; a med shelf holds heals; a bench holds attachments; an ordnance crate holds throwables; an ammo crate holds loose stacks. An energy gun carries its own magazines, so its rack holds another attachment where the ammo would be. The counts are [fewest, most] and include both ends, the chances are per spot, and the weights are per tier: a richer place leans towards racks and benches, a thin one towards shelves and crates.
_density_targets: What the whole floor should hold in one match, counted over sixty seeds in tools/checks/loot-tiers.ts. These exist because the move to typed spots re-tuned the floor without anyone noticing: guns fell 57 per cent, helmets 80, hop-ups 69, and magazines went up eight times, so the commonest object on the map after a heal was a magazine, most of them worse than the one already fitted. Every check passed, because they all asked whether a place hands you a gun and none asked how many. The numbers below are what the floor held before typed spots, with guns and the total a little higher because the owner asked for more of both. A spot kind's weights are free to move inside them; a change that takes the floor outside one is a balance decision and should be made on purpose.
_kinds: The single-item roll, which the floor no longer uses: the spot kinds above lay the floor out. It still says what one loose item is when something needs one on its own, and tools/verify.ts holds the rarity table to account through it. Weapon is weighted up because landing with no gun while three bots land near you was the whole of a match.
_mags: a magazine that comes out of a rack or a bench matches the rarity it rolled: white 1, blue 2, purple 3, gold 4. gunMag is the magazine a gun is already wearing when you find it, which is why the good ones are worth picking up off the floor as they lie.
_helmet: a helmet on the floor is gold this often, and mythic the rest of the time
_ammo: the types that lie about as a loose stack. There is no energy stack to find: energy guns carry their own magazines (src/config/ammo.json), which is also where the stack sizes live so there is one place to change them.
_bots: a bot lands unarmed and searches this long before it has its gun and a shield (ours)
_pods: a care package lands inside the next ring in rounds 2 to 4, falling this long (ours: Apex's fall time is not published)
